## `domain:ui` PM seat — claimed and dispatched

Session `session_01KbJQ1y1J12nZxYzFWhP8Q3` · branch `claude/issue-7636-plugin-development-guide-tombstones`

This card was filed **unassigned and unlabelled**; I have labelled it into the `domain:ui` lane and claimed it. **Comment thread read before ruling: zero comments, so no prior ruling exists and the disposition is the PM's to pick.**

### Disposition: part 1 only

The card proposes two parts. I am dispatching **part 1** and explicitly **not** part 2.

**Part 1 — in scope.** Correct the five members in the `os:check` fence of `skills/objectui/guides/plugin-development.md` to record that `inputType` / `min` / `max` / `step` / `placeholder` are ADR-0049 retirement tombstones, and point at `description` as the published remedy. This is a published-docs defect with blast radius **outside this repo** — the guide is copied into users' repositories — and it teaches a write that is now a `tsc` error at the authoring site and a named parse refusal at runtime.

**Part 2 — out of scope, file it instead.** "Should a fence that re-declares a published type be allowed to claim it" is a change to a **gate**, not to a document, and the card itself says the same shape probably exists in other guides. That is a separate measurement with a separate blast radius. Measure how many fences repo-wide re-declare a published type, file that as its own card, and do not change `check:skill-examples` in this PR.

### Sequence — this one has a hard dependency

Four of the five keys were tombstoned 2026-08-31 and are correctable today. The fifth, `inputType`, is tombstoned by **#5905 / PR #7639**, which is **in the merge queue as I write this**. Branch only from a `main` that already carries it, and verify by reading the `?: never` on `packages/types/src/base.ts` and the `retirementTombstone()` on the Zod mirror rather than by trusting this sentence. Writing all five before #7639 lands would document a tombstone that does not yet exist.

### Landing route — read this before you plan the PR

`skills/**` is a **governed surface**: agent drafts, human merges. This PR does **not** go through the merge queue on my authority and I will not enqueue it. Open it as a draft, leave it green, and say so in your report — the park is the expected outcome here, not a failure. The published skills tree also carries a **line-count ratchet**; stay inside it or state the number you moved it by and why.

### The gate question is the load-bearing half of your report

`pnpm check:skill-examples` is **green on this fence today** and will stay green after your fix, because the snippet compiles its own local `type ComponentInput` alias instead of importing the published one. So the gate cannot tell your corrected text from the wrong text. **Do not report a green gate as evidence your change is right.** Prove the correction against the real declarations in `packages/types/src/base.ts` and `packages/types/src/zod/base.zod.ts`, and run a two-arm control: show that a deliberately wrong edit to that fence also passes, which is the finding. That measurement is what justifies the part-2 card.

### Clause-② determination: **no** — but say so yourself

Documentation only; no schema, no export, no accept/reject behaviour moves. Make your own determination and label both carriers if you disagree.

## PM review — PR #7647 accepted, **parked for a human merge**

Part 1 delivered as ruled; part 2 measured and filed as **#7646**, now triaged into the `domain:ui` queue. `Clause-②: no`, and the dev reached that determination independently rather than deferring to mine — correct on the reasoning it gave: the tombstones and their named refusals already exist and already behave this way; this only stops the docs contradicting them.

**This PR is NOT enqueued and will not be.** `skills/**` is a governed surface — agent drafts, human merges. It is green and parked. That is the expected outcome, not a failure.

### The dependency was verified, not trusted

I told this dispatch that PR #7639 was mid-queue and that it must branch only from a `main` carrying the `inputType` tombstone. It did not take my word for it: it confirmed `origin/main` **is** `1ec291c0`, the #7639 merge commit, and read `inputType?: never` at `packages/types/src/base.ts:580` alongside `min`/`max`/`step`/`placeholder`, plus the `retirementTombstone()` entry on `ComponentInputSchema`, **before** branching. That is exactly the handling every base sha in a brief deserves.

### The green gate is explicitly not offered as evidence — which was the whole point

`check:skill-examples` is green on this fence **before and after**. The dev said so up front and proved the correction by other means:

- **`tsc`** importing the real `ComponentInput`, run **twice** — once resolved to the published `packages/types/dist/base.d.ts`, once to `packages/types/src/base.ts`, with `--listFiles` used to confirm which declaration was actually read. Identical results both arms: `TS2322` on all five keys.
- **Zod** — `ComponentInputSchema.safeParse` refused all five with `code=invalid_type`, each path naming the key and carrying its own remedy string.
- **Lit control, 2 of 2 on both instruments:** `advanced` and `description` — genuinely writable — compile clean and parse **accepted**.

And an earlier build of that instrument **was dark**: it resolved no module and failed all seven probes *including the controls*. The dev discarded that reading and rebuilt it with an explicit declaration path rather than publishing its zeros. That is the second time today a dark instrument was caught and discarded instead of reported (the other was on #7155). This is the habit that matters most.

### The missed prediction, reported as a miss

Worth preserving in full, because the honest reading is the opposite of the flattering one.

The first arm B left the corrected `inputType?: never` in place **and also** added `inputType?: string`. Predicted green; it went **red** — `TS2300 Duplicate identifier`, `TS2717`. The dev's own reading: that is the gate correctly catching an internally **invalid** snippet, and it says nothing about drift — *"my mutation was contaminated, not the gate stronger than claimed."*

It then rebuilt arm B as an **internally consistent lie** — `name: number` where the real member is `name: string`, all five tombstones restored as writable, plus an invented member `frobnicate` that exists on no type — and *that* passed **green**. Only the second arm measures the intended thing.

That distinction is the entire finding. A contaminated mutation that happens to go red would have looked like a passing control and would have buried the defect.

### Ratchet and changeset, both handled without prompting

Net **+7 lines** on both required readings — the edited file 446 → 453 and the whole published bundle 4495 → 4502 — and nothing was rewrapped or re-flowed to buy them. The +7 buys the tombstone block including the costly-to-confuse distinction that `BaseSchema.placeholder` is a **different key** and is unaffected. Worth the lines.

No changeset owed (docs-only), cited from the gate's own verdict line rather than asserted. And `skip-changeset` was correctly **not** applied — in this repo that label reads nothing and exempts nothing.

### #7646 came back stronger than the brief asked for

I asked for a count of fences that re-declare a published type. The answer generalises the defect properly: **26 fences**, spanning **both** gates — 3 of the 13 `os:check`-marked fences (23% of everything `check:skill-examples` judges) plus 18 under `content/docs` where `check:doc-snippets` is opt-out rather than opt-in. Census lit control: the count of marked fences (13) matches the number the gate prints for itself.

Dedup was searched first, and when the global search endpoint returned zero it was treated as a **dark instrument** — the endpoint is blocked in these sessions — discarded, and re-run through the repo-scoped list plus local grep where the control lit. Confirmed distinct from #6172, #7493 and #5465.
